conversation.content:
Hello there—thank you for taking a few minutes to talk with me today. I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician, which simply means I specialize in the emotional changes that can come with new motherhood. To get a quick snapshot of how you’ve been feeling lately, I’m going to run through the EPDS (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale) with you. It’s a short 10-item questionnaire that looks at mood, anxiety, and—importantly—whether you’re having any thoughts that feel too heavy to manage alone. Everything you share stays between us unless safety is a concern, and we’ll go at your pace. When you’re ready, we’ll start with the first question:

Over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

*shifts in chair, eyes down for a moment*

Not really... I mean, sometimes my husband will try to make a joke to lighten the mood, and I might give a little smile, but it's not like before. Things that used to make me laugh out loud... now they just feel kind of flat. I watched a show last night that I used to love and I just felt... nothing.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really… I mean, maybe a little chuckle here or there when my husband tries to be silly, but mostly I just feel kind of numb to it. It’s like the joy doesn’t quite reach me the way it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

*quietly*  
Hardly at all… I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower. Now it feels like I’m just getting through the day. Sometimes I think, “Maybe tomorrow I’ll enjoy something,” but when tomorrow comes, it’s the same heaviness.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

*nods slowly, eyes wet*

Yeah... I do that a lot. When the baby won't stop crying, I keep thinking it's because I'm not doing something right, like I'm failing him somehow. Yesterday I spilled a little breastmilk and just sat there crying, telling myself I'm a terrible mom over something so small. My head knows accidents happen, but I still feel like everything that goes wrong is somehow my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

*wrings hands in lap*  
Most of the time. Even when everything’s calm, my mind races—Is the baby breathing? Did I sterilize the bottle right? What if I trip on the stairs? It’s like a loop I can’t switch off. I’ll check the monitor three, four times, then still stand over the crib watching his chest rise. There’s no real reason, but the worry feels glued to me.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes… a couple of times this week. I’ll be feeding the baby and suddenly my heart starts racing and I feel like I can’t breathe. Nothing’s happening—no noise, nothing wrong—but it feels like something awful is about to happen. It passes after a few minutes, but it leaves me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

*nods, voice shaky*

Yeah... most days it feels like I'm drowning in small stuff. The dishes pile up, the baby needs changing, I haven't showered... and it all feels impossible. Yesterday I just sat on the floor while he cried, staring at the mess, thinking "I can't do this." I eventually got up and managed, but it's like climbing a mountain just to get through basic things.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

*looks down, pulling cardigan tighter*

Yes… most nights I lie there feeling this heavy sadness even though the baby’s finally asleep. My mind keeps listing everything I think I did wrong that day, or imagining awful things that could happen to him. I’ll stare at the ceiling for an hour or two, then jerk awake every time I hear a little grunt from the crib. It’s like my body’s exhausted but my brain won’t let me rest.
I have felt sad or miserable

*nods slowly, eyes glassy*

Yes… pretty much every day. It’s like there’s this gray cloud that follows me around. Even when I’m holding the baby and he smiles, the sadness is still underneath—this empty, achy feeling. Some mornings I wake up and my first thought is, *“I can’t do another day like this.”* I keep hoping it’ll lift, but it hasn’t.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

*voice cracks, eyes welling up*

Yeah… I’ve cried twice this week. Once was when the baby wouldn’t settle and I just felt so useless. The other time I was folding his tiny onesies and this wave of sadness just hit me out of nowhere. I sat on the nursery floor sobbing into a pile of clean laundry, feeling like I’m failing him even though I’m trying so hard.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

*hesitates, twisting the hem of her sweater*

It… it has crossed my mind. Not like a plan or anything—I’d never leave my baby—but when things feel really heavy, I’ll think, “What if I just wasn’t here?” It’s fleeting, just a flash, maybe once or twice this week. I push it away because I know I need to be here for him, but the thought does show up.

You've shared how the joy that used to come easily now feels out of reach, replaced by a heavy, gray sadness that follows you through each day. Simple tasks feel overwhelming, worry loops constantly in your mind, and moments of tearfulness catch you off guard. You described feeling numb to things you once loved, blaming yourself for every small mishap, and fleeting thoughts of not wanting to be here-yet you're fighting to stay present for your baby.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 26, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient reports only occasional faint laughter and a pervasive numbness to joy, aligning with "Definitely not so much now."</sym>, <sym>Patient explicitly states "Hardly at all" and describes anhedonia with loss of anticipatory pleasure, matching the highest severity option.</sym>, <sym>Patient reports frequent, intense self-blame for minor incidents, matching 'Yes, most of the time</sym>, <sym>Patient describes pervasive, intrusive worries occurring "most of the time" with compulsive checking behaviors, matching "Yes, very often"</sym>, <sym>The patient describes unexpected episodes of intense physical fear ('heart racing, can't breathe, feels like something awful is about to happen') occurring a couple of times this week, matching 'Yes, sometimes'.</sym>, <sym>Patient describes feeling overwhelmed 'most days,' unable to manage basic tasks, and immobilized by stress, matching 'most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>Patient reports nightly difficulty sleeping due to persistent sadness and intrusive thoughts, matching "Yes, most of the time".</sym>, <sym>Response conveys pervasive, daily sadness with persistent low mood and hopelessness</sym>, <sym>Patient describes crying twice this week due to overwhelming sadness and feelings of inadequacy, matching 'Yes, quite often</sym>)
**Reasoning:** Score ≥14 plus endorsement of item 10 indicates high likelihood of <med>major depressive disorder with peripartum onset</med>; patient meets core criteria: daily low mood, marked loss of interest, fatigue, guilt, impaired functioning, and passive self-harm ideation without plan. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange same-day urgent appointment with <med>perinatal mental health specialist</med> or <med>primary care provider</med> for full evaluation and safety planning
2. Call local crisis line or 988 if thoughts of self-harm intensify; keep numbers visible
3. Share these results and your feelings with a trusted support person who can stay with you tonight
4. Begin gentle schedule of daytime rest, hydration, and 10-minute outdoor light exposure; accept help with housework and night feeds
5. Schedule re-screen within 48 hours to monitor symptom trajectory and treatment response
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, ≤ 1 yr after delivery (est.)  
Date: [today]

A. Primary symptom endorsements  
• Persistent low mood, anhedonia, daily crying spells  
• Marked guilt / self-blame (“bad mom” cognitions)  
• excessive, uncontrolled worry; panic episodes (racing heart, breathlessness)  
• Overwhelm / inability to complete routine tasks  
• Sleep-onset and maintenance problems linked to ruminative thoughts  
• Passive suicidal ideation (no plan, intent, or means)

B. Pattern summary  
All 10 items on EPDS-equivalent probe endorsed at clinically significant level; cluster most consistent with moderate–severe postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety.

C. Screening risk flags  
• Passive self-harm thoughts reported → safety issue; needs immediate risk assessment  
• Functional impairment (self-care, infant care, household tasks)  
• Physiological stress (sleep deprivation, panic symptoms) potentially compounding emotional liability

D. Clinical impression (screening only)  
High likelihood of major postpartum depressive episode with anxious features; rule-out postpartum anxiety disorder; urgent referral to perinatal mental health specialist and same-day safety planning recommended.

E. Next steps documented  
Discussed: voluntary referral to OB mental-health team, crisis hotline numbers, support person notification; follow-up within 24–48 hr scheduled.
